facts: Newport defines deep work as professional activities performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that push cognitive capabilities to their limit, create new value, improve skill and are hard to replicate.

Shallow work is non-cognitively demanding, logistical-style tasks, often done while distracted, such as answering email, attending status meetings and filling out forms; it tends not to create much new value and is easy to replicate.
The formula: High-Quality Work Produced = (Time Spent) x (Intensity of Focus).
Newport says experts max out around four hours of deep work a day, beginners far less.
scene_details: the email inbox, the status meeting and the form as shallow work
the formula time spent times intensity of focus
four hours a day as an expert's ceiling
tension: Two people can sit at a desk for the same hours and produce very different amounts, because focus is a multiplier.
opening_idea: Open on the formula: time spent multiplied by intensity of focus.

lessons.idea: Hours at the desk are only half of the output equation; the focus attached to them is the other half, so protecting a few intense hours can beat many scattered ones.
lessons.anchor: output = time spent x intensity of focus; experts reach about four hours a day

reflect_final: Which task on this week's list actually needs your full focus, and what would you move out of its way to give it a clean hour?

use_cases.situation: Your team fills the day with status meetings
use_cases.move: Cite Newport's point that output is time times focus and propose one meeting-free morning for the work that needs thinking.

use_cases.situation: You answer email in the same hour you plan to write
use_cases.move: Move email to the end of the block and let the first hour go to the hard task.

use_cases.situation: A colleague asks for a quick question during your focused hour
use_cases.move: Say you are in the middle of something and give a time when you can answer.

pocket_idea: Output is time multiplied by focus, so one hour with no inbox can outweigh three scattered ones.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Newport's formula is time spent times intensity of focus, so a distracted hour counts for less than it looks.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Cal Newport splits work in two. Deep work is distraction-free effort that stretches your skill and is hard to copy. Shallow work is email, status meetings and forms. His formula: quality equals time spent times intensity of focus. Experts, he says, top out around four deep hours a day.
